issues.title: Convention: a refusal must say whether it is a rule or a stub
issues.body:
## The observation

From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Onboarding a hire costs 3 Attention. With a full queue, one
option behaves correctly, but the other says:

> insufficient capacity to handle by cannibalising - pick another option

Pip:

> which, like, isn't strictly true?

and then the part that generalises:

> if its because we haven't built it, we should also say **[ALPHA: This behaviour is a stub, harass the developers to extend it!]**

## The principle, which is bigger than the string

**A stub that refuses in the voice of a rule teaches the player a rule that does not exist.**

"You cannot do that" and "we have not built that yet" are different statements. The first
is worldbuilding -- something the player is meant to learn, plan around, and still believe
at 1.0. The second is an apology. Conflating them is a specific kind of lie to the player,
and it is the in-game cousin of the false-claim problem this estate spent two days auditing
on the website (`docs/CLAIM_AUDIT_2026-08-06.md`).

**An alpha is allowed to be incomplete. It is not allowed to present incompleteness as design.**

## He was right about this one, and for a deeper reason than the wording

Traced, not guessed:

- `MonthPlan.pay_by_cannibalizing()` can only free Attention by cancelling entries in
  `MonthPlan.queued_strategic`.
- `queued_strategic` is written only by `MonthPlan.queue_strategic()`.
- Its sole production wrapper, `GameManager.queue_strategic_action()`, has **zero callers**.
  The only callers of `queue_strategic()` anywhere are unit tests and the `tests/manual/`
  sim harness.
- The queue the player can actually SEE is `GameState.queued_actions`, filled by
  `GameManager.select_action()`, which charges Attention by incrementing `attention_spent`
  directly and never mints a `queued_strategic` entry.

So in the shipped game the "pull from planned work" option can never pull from planned
work -- its WIP registry has no producer, and the visible queue is invisible to it. The
refusal explained a budget where the truth was an absence. Pip's instinct was exactly
right: it isn't strictly true.

(`QueueGantt.rows_from_state()` renders `queued_strategic` as the "strategic WIP" lane of
the on-screen gantt, so that lane is also always empty. The player's planned work shows up
only via the separate "planned" tentative rows.)

## The convention

Implemented in the linked PR; recorded here because the convention outlives the fix.

Every refusal is exactly one of two kinds, and the code must say which:

| kind | meaning | ships as |
|---|---|---|
| **RULE** | a real game constraint | the sentence, unmarked |
| **STUB** | refuses because the behaviour is unbuilt | the sentence + Pip's `[ALPHA: ...]` marker |

There is deliberately **no third constructor**. A refusal that states a reason which is not
the actual reason ("WRONG") is a defect to fix at the call site, not a category to ship.

### Why it should resist rot

The `_facts_this_copy_must_not_break` block rotted because it relied on remembering. Three
independent properties here do not:

1. **The classification is a required choice, not a remembered step.** `Refusal.rule()` and
   `Refusal.stub()` are the only constructors. There is no unclassified one to fall into.
2. **The marker expires on its own.** It is gated on `BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA` -- the
   existing era switch already documented "flip false at 1.0". No stub marker can survive
   into the finished game by being forgotten; one flip retires all of them.
3. **A ratchet, not a plea.** `tools/check_refusal_classification.py` fails any refusal that
   is neither classified nor in `tools/refusal_baseline.txt`, and that baseline may only
   shrink. New debt cannot be added silently; and because the baseline is keyed on the
   message text, *rewording* an old refusal knocks it out of the baseline too -- touching an
   old lie makes you classify it.

Plus a fourth, specific to the fix: the cannibalize discriminator is **derived, not
declared**. It classifies as STUB exactly when nothing was cannibalisable, so the day
anyone wires `queue_strategic_action()` into the UI, the marker retires itself and the
genuine RULE takes over. Nobody has to remember to switch it off. `test_refusal_stub_vs_rule.gd`
pins both halves.

### It extends prior art rather than competing with it

Searched first. Three existing half-conventions, now subsumed rather than paralleled:

- `is_stub: true` + `[Coming Soon]` in `godot/data/actions/travel.json`, consumed by
  `travel_panel_controller.gd`. That marks an **action** as unbuilt *before* the player
  presses. `Refusal` marks a **refusal** as unbuilt *after* they press. Different moments,
  both wanted. (This is `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md` item 5, open pending a keep-vs-hide ruling.)
- `ALPHA_TOOLS_TOGGLE_WARNING` / `ALPHA_TOOLS_GAME_OVER_NOTICE` in `game_config.gd` -- the
  settled wording for dev powers. Same era switch, same ASCII bracket chrome, different
  subject.
- `BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA` -- reused as the expiry gate rather than inventing a second
  era switch.

## Open follow-ups this convention exposes but does not close

1. **The option label is still a promise the game cannot keep.** `hiring_pipeline.gd` offers
   "Set them up now (N Att, pull from planned work)" and "Mentor them (N Att, pull from
   planned work)". Marking the refusal stops the lie at the moment of refusal; the *offer*
   still names a mechanic with no producer. That needs a rewrite, not a correction, and the
   copy is Pip's -- proposed, not done.
2. **The real fix is to build it, or to remove the verb.** Either wire
   `queue_strategic_action()` into the plan screen so "planned work" means the queue the
   player sees, or collapse the two HANDLE verbs to one until it does.
3. **`advertise` is greyed "SOON" on the action bar while the same mechanic ships enabled
   one panel away** (`action_bar_renderer.gd` `COMING_SOON_ACTION_IDS` vs
   `hiring_panel_controller.gd`). The refusal is false: it refuses because of a hardcoded
   list, not because the feature is missing. Behaviour change, needs a design call.
4. **`employee_screen.gd` delivers a refusal to a method that does not exist**
   (`game_manager.has_method("add_message")` is false), so confirming "Fire" with
   insufficient severance closes the dialog and says nothing at all. A silent refusal is the
   limit case of this whole issue.
5. **`DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md` cannot currently be committed to.** The matching entry for its
   "On honesty and legibility" section was written and then reverted: the file carries 185
   pre-existing non-ASCII characters (85 em-dashes, 81 arrows, 14 ellipses) and the
   BLOCKING `enforce-standards` pre-commit hook rejects it on line 1. Editing the doc where
   design principles are supposed to be recorded therefore requires either a 185-character
   sweep of Pip's prose or `--no-verify`. That is its own anti-rot failure and wants its own
   decision (sweep it, or exempt legacy docs), so it is reported rather than papered over.

6. **The guard covers one shape only.** It detects the `{"success": false, ...}` Dictionary
   form. Bare rejection strings (`error_occurred.emit(...)`, UI labels, disabled-button
   tooltips) are audited by hand and not gated. Stated in the tool's docstring so nobody
   trusts it further than it goes.

issues.title: feat(copy): a refusal must say whether it is a rule or a stub
issues.body:
Closes nothing; implements the convention filed as #1221.

## What Pip saw

Onboarding a hire costs 3 Attention. With a full queue, **Q** (pay from reserve) worked and
**W** refused:

> `[!] Insufficient capacity to handle by cannibalizing -- pick another option.`

> *"which, like, isn't strictly true?"*

> *"if its because we haven't built it, we should also say [ALPHA: This behaviour is a stub, harass the developers to extend it!]"*

## What the message actually is

**A stub, not a rule** -- and for a deeper reason than the wording. Traced, not guessed:

- The card is `HiringPipeline.build_onboard_prompt()`. Its 3 Attention is exactly
  `laptop(1) + systems(1) + meet_people(1)` from `ONBOARD_ATTENTION`.
- `Q` = `provision_reserve` -> `handle_reserve`; `W` = `provision_cannibalize`
  ("Set them up now (3 Att, pull from planned work)") -> `handle_cannibalize`.
- `MonthPlan.pay_by_cannibalizing()` frees Attention **only** by cancelling entries in
  `MonthPlan.queued_strategic`.
- `queued_strategic` is written only by `MonthPlan.queue_strategic()`, whose sole production
  wrapper `GameManager.queue_strategic_action()` has **zero callers**. Every caller anywhere
  is a unit test or the `tests/manual/` sim harness.
- The queue the player can *see* is `GameState.queued_actions`, filled by
  `GameManager.select_action()`, which charges Attention by incrementing `attention_spent`
  directly and never mints a `queued_strategic` entry.

So "pull from planned work" cannot reach the planned work. Its WIP registry has no producer,
and the visible queue is invisible to it. `Q` worked because the reserve is a separate pool
the cannibalize path never touches. The refusal explained a budget where the truth was an
absence.

Reproduce the dead end:

```
rg -n 'queue_strategic' godot/ --glob '!godot/tests/**'
```

Two hits, both the definition and its uncalled wrapper.

Side effect worth knowing: `QueueGantt.rows_from_state()` renders `queued_strategic` as the
gantt's "strategic WIP" lane, so that lane is always empty too.

## Audit: every refusal message in the game

Three sweeps (core+autoload, ui+scenes+data, and a prior-art search), each tracing the
producing code path rather than reading the string.

| | count |
|---|---|
| **RULE** -- real constraint, correctly stated | **106** |
| **STUB** -- refuses because the feature is unbuilt | **29** |
| **WRONG** -- states a reason that is not the actual reason | **8** |
| **UNCLEAR** -- could not determine from the code | **1** |
| total distinct refusal strings traced | **144** |

Split by tree: core + autoload 98 (71 RULE / 21 STUB / 6 WRONG / 0 UNCLEAR); ui + scenes +
data 46 (35 RULE / 8 STUB / 2 WRONG / 1 UNCLEAR).

**The headline is that the game is mostly honest.** 106 of 144 trace to genuine state, and
the affordability/idempotence guards in `hiring_pipeline`, `ledger`, `upgrades`, `events`,
`finance_engine` and `leaderboard_sync` are all correctly stated. The conflation Pip hit is
real but not endemic.

The one **UNCLEAR**, listed rather than guessed: `godot/data/actions/fundraising.json:22`
*"Aggressive funding - higher amounts but requires strong reputation"* -- `fundraise_big` has
an 8-reputation *cost* and a `reputation * 500` bonus, but no reputation *threshold* anywhere.
Cannot tell from the code whether the copy means the cost or a gate that was never built.

A caveat on the STUB count: several are **dead code** rather than live lies -- accurate
sentences on branches nothing can currently reach (`media_system.gd` is never instantiated at
all; the `unignorable` event flag has no producer in `godot/data/**`; the DEFER verb has no
production caller). Those want deletion or content, not markers, so they are reported in
#1221 rather than marked here. I deliberately did **not** classify a dead-but-true sentence as
a stub: if it fired, it would state a real rule.

## The convention

`godot/scripts/core/refusal.gd`. Two constructors, no third:

```gdscript
Refusal.rule(text)   # a real constraint -- ships unmarked
Refusal.stub(text)   # unbuilt -- appends Pip's [ALPHA: ...] marker
Refusal.mark_stub(text)  # for sites that build a bare string, not a result dict
```

WRONG is deliberately not a constructor: a refusal stating a reason that is not the actual
reason is a defect to fix at the call site, never a category to ship.

### Why it resists rot

The brief's bar was "hard to omit", explicitly against the way
`_facts_this_copy_must_not_break` decayed. Four independent mechanisms, none of which is
"remember to":

1. **The classification is a required choice.** You cannot construct a refusal through this
   API without naming `rule` or `stub`. There is no unclassified constructor to fall into.
2. **The marker expires on its own.** It is gated on `BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA` -- the
   existing switch already documented *"Flip false at 1.0"*. No stub marker can survive into
   the finished game by being forgotten; one flip retires every one of them. This reuses the
   era switch rather than inventing a second one.
3. **A ratchet, not a plea.** `tools/check_refusal_classification.py` (pre-commit +
   `quality-checks.yml`) fails any refusal that is neither classified nor in
   `tools/refusal_baseline.txt`. The baseline **may only shrink** -- `--write-baseline`
   refuses to write a larger one. And because the key is `path :: "message"`, *rewording* a
   baselined refusal knocks it out, so touching an old lie makes you classify it. It shipped
   **green over 70 pre-existing sites** on purpose: a gate that is red on arrival gets
   `--no-verify`-ed and then ignored forever (`UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md` rec. 3).
   It already shrank 72 -> 70 in this PR.
4. **The specific discriminator is derived, not declared.** The cannibalize refusal reads
   STUB exactly when `cancelled.is_empty()` -- i.e. when nothing was cannibalisable. The day
   anyone wires `queue_strategic_action()` up, the marker retires itself and the genuine RULE
   takes over. Nothing to remember to switch off.
   `test_cannibalize_refusal_becomes_a_rule_once_wip_exists` is the pin on that.

### It extends prior art rather than competing

Searched before inventing, per the brief. Found three half-conventions and subsumed them:

- **`is_stub: true` + `[Coming Soon]`** (`travel.json` -> `travel_panel_controller.gd`) marks
  an *action* unbuilt *before* the press; `Refusal` marks a *refusal* unbuilt *after*.
  Different moments, both wanted. (`TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md` item 5 is the open keep-vs-hide
  ruling for the former.)
- **`ALPHA_TOOLS_TOGGLE_WARNING` / `ALPHA_TOOLS_GAME_OVER_NOTICE`** (`game_config.gd`) -- the
  settled wording for dev powers. Same era switch, same ASCII bracket chrome, different
  subject.
- **`BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA`** -- reused as the expiry gate.

The checker follows `tools/check_scene_nav.py`'s shape exactly (`Layer: PROVE`, no argparse,
dual full-tree/changed-files mode, an inline `# refusal: <kind> -- <why>` escape hatch, exit
0/1) and declares itself in the generated `docs/TOOLS.md`.

## What changed

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/core/refusal.gd` | **new.** The contract, the marker, the era gate. |
| `godot/scripts/core/window_resolver.gd` | The fix Pip found. Classifies the cannibalize refusal STUB when nothing was cannibalisable, RULE when WIP was really eaten and still fell short. |
| `godot/scripts/core/office.gd` | STUB. `apply_upgrade`'s "No such office upgrade" *always* fires (`offices.json` ships `"upgrades": []`), so it read as "you named a bad id" when the truth was "the catalogue is empty". Same derived discriminator. |
| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd` | WRONG. `if is_stub: can_afford = false` routed unbuilt options through the *unaffordable* branch, which also greys the on-face price -- so `send_delegation`, which costs nothing, rendered its own "Free" label as if unpayable. Two refusals, one costume. Affordability is now honest for every option; unbuilt options still disable the button but keep a truthful price and say they are unbuilt. |
| `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd` | Presentation only: lifts the marker onto its own line so Pip's "-- pick another option." stays attached to the reason. |
| `tools/check_refusal_classification.py` + `tools/refusal_baseline.txt` | The ratchet. |
| `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.github/workflows/quality-checks.yml`, `docs/TOOLS.md` | Wiring. |
| `godot/tests/unit/test_refusal_stub_vs_rule.gd` | **new**, 9 tests. |

**No copy was restyled.** Every existing sentence is byte-identical; the marker is appended.

## Proposed, not done

Left for Pip or a design call, per "where a string needs a real rewrite rather than a
correction, propose it and leave the original":

1. **The option label is still a promise the game cannot keep.** `hiring_pipeline.gd` offers
   *"Set them up now (N Att, pull from planned work)"* and the mentoring twin. Marking the
   refusal stops the lie at refusal-time; the *offer* still names a mechanic with no producer.
   The real fix is to build it (wire `queue_strategic_action()` into the plan screen) or drop
   the verb until it exists.
2. **Six WRONG refusals in `hiring_pipeline.gd` conflate money and Attention.**
   `_pay_onboard(state, money, att)` returns a bare `false` for *either* shortfall and each
   call site hardcodes one guess. Laptop (`:474`) and visa (`:482`) cost both but name only
   money, so an Attention-blocked player is told to find cash; systems/meet_people/mentoring
   cost $0, so a negative balance reports as an Attention shortage; and `:660` can only render
   as *"Can't afford the mentoring budget ($0)."* Fix: have `_pay_onboard` return *which*
   resource failed. That needs new sentences, so it is proposed, not written.
3. **`actions.gd:569`** *"No financiers are interested right now (reputation/standing too
   low)."* is WRONG and dead: the `desperation` instrument has `min_rep: 0` and no gates, so
   `generate_offers()` is never empty except on a data-load failure. It teaches a reputation
   gate that does not exist.
4. **`advertise` is greyed "SOON" on the action bar while the same mechanic ships enabled one
   panel away** (`action_bar_renderer.gd` `COMING_SOON_ACTION_IDS` vs
   `hiring_panel_controller.gd:90-96`). It refuses because of a hardcoded list, not because
   the feature is missing. Behaviour change; needs a design call.
5. **`employee_screen.gd:83` sends its refusal to a method that does not exist**
   (`game_manager.has_method("add_message")` is false), so confirming "Fire" without severance
   closes the dialog and says nothing at all. A silent refusal is the limit case of this issue.
6. **Dead-code clusters** to delete rather than mark: `media_system.gd` (never instantiated;
   9 refusals), `actions.gd:989/993/1007` (dead duplicates of the live `ConferenceTrip` path),
   and the `unignorable`-gated refusals whose flag no content sets -- which also means the
   "a crisis drags you home from the conference early" beat can never fire.
7. **`DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md` cannot currently be committed to.** The matching entry for its
   "On honesty and legibility" section was written and reverted: the file has 185 pre-existing
   non-ASCII characters and the blocking `enforce-standards` hook rejects it on line 1. Editing
   the doc where design principles are recorded needs either a 185-char sweep of Pip's prose or
   `--no-verify`. Reported rather than papered over.

## Coordination

Stayed out of `main_ui.gd` entirely -- `_on_dynamic_action_pressed()` belongs to the
`fix/submenu-rejection-visibility` lane. Its two refusals were audited (both RULE, correctly
stated) and left untouched. No file in this PR overlaps that branch.

## Tests

```
python3 scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300
```

**1322 tests, 0 failures** (baseline 1313 + 9 new), 131/131 files collected.

The gate proves it can return the other answer:
`python3 tools/check_refusal_classification.py --self-test` exercises all six classified
forms plus an unclassified refusal plus a comment-that-mentions-a-refusal, and is run in CI
before the real scan.

`Ladder-Impact: none -- message text plus a `refusal` classification key on failure paths,
and a UI grey-out split. No cost, effect, RNG, resolution outcome or scoring change.`

Do not merge -- for Pip's review.

issues.body:
Fixes #1219.

**Do not merge yet** -- a release tag may happen this afternoon and this may or may not make it.
Flagged for Pip's call.

## The bug

`_on_dynamic_action_pressed()` returns at its `is_submenu` branch, which sits **above** the
attention/affordability guards and the `report_rejection()` calls that make a refusal visible.
#1204 re-armed those guards inside `SubmenuController.on_option_selected()`, covering the six
icon-grid panels plus financing -- but the two BESPOKE panels never queue through it. Hiring and
travel call the `GameManager.hiring_*` / `GameActions` conference delegates directly and rendered
the backend's refusal with a bare `log_message()`, i.e. into `WatchScreen`'s feed, which
`ScreenModeController` hides for the whole of PLAN.

Playtest repro, verbatim:

> I can fail silently if I queue 19 fundraisings and then try to make offers to 2 people. Making
> offers doesn't show up as a card.

Pre-existing gap, not a regression.

## How many child-click paths, and where the check went

Eleven child-click buttons hang off the `is_submenu` early return, in four panel families
reaching the commit through three chokepoints:

| # | family | child clicks | chokepoint | before this PR |
|---|--------|--------------|------------|----------------|
| 1 | six icon-grid panels | per-option buttons | `SubmenuController.on_option_selected` | covered by #1204 |
| 2 | financing (list layout) | per-option buttons | `SubmenuController.on_option_selected` | covered by #1204 |
| 3 | hiring | 6 (advertise / connections / interview / onboard step / skip mentoring / send offer) | `HiringPanelController._hiring_action_result` | **silent** |
| 4 | travel | 4 (delegation stub / submit paper / attend conference / conference trip) | 4 separate leaf commits | **silent**, except the trip |

The travel *trip* leaf was already visible -- `GameManager.attend_conference_trip` emits
`error_occurred`, which is the same door. It is deliberately left alone and commented, because
routing it through the new door too would raise the toast twice for one click.

**The check went to child selection, at the chokepoints -- not above the early return.** The
submenu driver is free; the child inside the menu carries the cost. Hoisting the guards would
refuse to *open* a menu the player is entitled to browse, which is a worse bug than this one.
`test_the_submenu_branch_still_returns_above_the_affordability_guards` now pins that ordering so
it cannot be "fixed" by a later reader.

Because all six hiring handlers already funnelled through `_hiring_action_result`, hiring needed
**one line**. Travel's leaves cannot share a chokepoint of their own (each calls a different
delegate), so they share the **host's** door -- the decision about what a refusal looks like
still lives in exactly one place.

## The one door

```gdscript
EventResultPresenter.present_outcome(result, verb) -> bool   # exposed as MainUI.report_outcome
```

Acceptance keeps the cyan feed line the panels already wrote; refusal goes out through the same
`present_error()` as every other rejection, so it reaches the PLAN toast **and** the feed. It
returns `result.success`, so a call site can gate its follow-up on the backend having actually
accepted (#821 -- no phantom tiles). A refusal with no message still names the action rather than
raising a blank toast.

**The refusal reason is relayed from the backend verbatim, on purpose.** A shadow pre-check in
the view is exactly the defect #1204 fixed, and only the backend knows whether a click failed for
Attention, money, reputation, desk space or pipeline state. It already answers in house voice
with the number -- `"Not enough Attention to make an offer (1 needed)"` -- the same shape as the
view's own `"Not enough Attention: need %d %s hours, have %d"`.

## The two cases called out in the brief

* **Cumulative queue** (the actual repro): `MonthPlan.available()` nets out what is already
  committed, so 19 queued fundraisings are what refuse the 1-Attention offer, not the offer's own
  cost. Already correct in the backend, and it charges nothing for a refused spend.
  `test_the_cumulative_queue_is_what_refuses_the_offer_not_the_offers_own_cost` pins this, so the
  presentation fix can never be "corrected" into a view-side re-derivation of the rule that then
  drifts.
* **Already-queued action becomes unaffordable**: the submenu buttons disable off a snapshot, so
  a button can look live and still be refused. That refusal now reports, whatever its reason.

## No gameplay change

Same conditions, same early returns, same economy. `tools/check_ladder_bump.py` reports
**0 gameplay-surface files changed**. Ladder-Impact: none -- UI presentation only.

## RED before green (TESTING_STRATEGY.md)

`python3 scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300`

| stage | result |
|-------|--------|
| baseline, `origin/main` | **1313 tests, 0 failures** |
| tests only, production code untouched (commit `968b5c0d`) | **1324 tests, 9 failures** |
| with the fix (commit `d9756da5`) | **1324 tests, 0 failures** |

The nine RED failures, from the JUnit XML of that run:

```
test_a_refused_hiring_child_click_reaches_the_player_not_the_hidden_feed
    [0] expected to equal [1]:  the refused offer is reported through the PLAN-visible door, not swallowed
test_an_accepted_hiring_child_click_still_confirms_through_the_same_door
    [0] expected to equal [1]:  the acceptance goes out the same one door
test_hiring_refusals_are_fixed_at_one_chokepoint_not_six_buttons
    the chokepoint routes the backend verdict through the host's one result door
test_travel_child_clicks_report_through_the_same_one_door
    travel's backend results go out the same door as hiring's
test_a_travel_click_that_cannot_do_anything_says_so
    [0] expected to equal [1]:  a click that cannot land is refused where the player can see it
test_present_outcome_is_the_one_door_for_a_backend_verdict
    EventResultPresenter owns the one backend-result door
test_present_outcome_confirms_an_acceptance_without_raising_a_rejection
    EventResultPresenter owns the one backend-result door
test_present_outcome_never_refuses_in_silence
    EventResultPresenter owns the one backend-result door
test_main_ui_exposes_the_outcome_door_the_bespoke_panels_report_through
    MainUI keeps the backend-result door next to report_rejection
```

Two of the eleven new tests pass on unmodified `main`, deliberately: the one pinning that the
`is_submenu` return stays above the guards, and the one pinning that `MonthPlan` already refuses
the cumulative overbook correctly. They are there to stop the fix being taken in the wrong
direction, not to go red.

The simulation tier was not run: this touches `godot/scripts/ui/` only, no
simulation/economy/replay code (CLAUDE.md).

## One unrelated commit, and why it is here

`176d2fec` regenerates `docs/calendar/`. It is **not** part of the fix -- it is carried because
it **blocks** it. The pre-commit `commitment-calendar-check` hook fails on any commit touching a
scanned file, and it already fails on a clean checkout of `origin/main`:

```
$ git worktree add --detach <tmp> origin/main
$ python3 scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py --check
Commitment calendar is STALE: docs/calendar/pdoom1-commitments.ics, docs/calendar/COMMITMENTS_INDEX.md
  computed: 48 declared + 4 release-train + 38 UNPARSED = 90 events; 0 malformed
  MISSING from the committed index: | 2026-08-10 | `docs/PRIVACY_POSTURE.md` | 25 |
```

issues.title: Submenu-driven actions fail silently: the is_submenu early return skips every rejection report (hiring is entirely on that path)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
## The repro, verbatim from the playtest

> I can fail silently if I queue 19 fundraisings and then try to make offers to 2 people. Making offers doesn't show up as a card.

Found in a live playtest, 2026-08-14.

## What is happening

`godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd`, `_on_dynamic_action_pressed()`:

```gdscript
var action = _get_action_by_id(action_id)
if action.get("is_submenu", false):
    _open_submenu(action_id)
    return                    # <-- returns HERE
```

The attention and affordability guards -- **and the `report_rejection()` calls that make a
refusal visible** -- sit *below* that early return. So the submenu-driven path never reaches
them.

#1204 re-armed those two guards inside `SubmenuController.on_option_selected()`, which covers
the six icon-grid panels plus financing. It did **not** cover the two BESPOKE panels, which
never queue through `on_option_selected` at all:

* **hiring** (`HiringPanelController`) calls the `GameManager.hiring_*` delegates directly
* **travel** (`TravelPanelController`) calls the `GameActions` conference delegates directly

Both rendered the backend's refusal with a bare `log_message()`. The feed lives inside
`WatchScreen`, which `ScreenModeController` hides for the whole of PLAN -- so the refusal was
written into a hidden node and the player saw nothing at all.

Hiring is entirely on that path: `action_bar_renderer.gd:83` lists `interview_next` and
`hire_best` in `HIDDEN_FROM_ACTION_BAR_IDS` as "no-target menu drivers", so hiring is only
reachable through the `hire_staff` submenu.

**Eleven child-click buttons** were affected: six hiring handlers (advertise / connections /
interview / onboard step / skip mentoring / send offer) and three travel leaf commits, plus the
`send_delegation` stub.

## Why the missing card is the same bug

Nothing is queued because nothing is *accepted* -- and that part is correct. The backend refuses
properly: 19 queued fundraisings exhaust the month plan, `MonthPlan.spend_attention(1)` returns
false, `HiringPipeline.make_offer` hands back
`{success: false, message: "Not enough Attention to make an offer (1 needed)"}` and charges
nothing. The economy is fine. What was broken is that the refusal, and its reason, never reached
a surface the player could see during PLAN.

## This is a pre-existing gap, not a regression

The bespoke panels have presented their results this way since CARVE 3 / CARVE 4 lifted them out
of the monolith. #1204 narrowed the hole; it did not close it.

## The design trap for whoever picks this up

**Do not simply move the affordability check above the early return.** The submenu *driver* is
free; the *child* inside the menu carries the cost. Guarding the driver would refuse to *open* a
menu the player is entitled to browse -- a worse bug than this one. The check belongs at child
selection, on the path that actually commits.

## Also in scope

* an action already queued that becomes unaffordable
* the child being affordable in isolation while the *cumulative* queue is not (this is the
  actual repro)
* no phantom tiles: #821's rule, the UI tile appears only when the backend accepts

## Fix

PR: see linked pull request. Fixed at the chokepoints rather than the eleven buttons: one new
door, `EventResultPresenter.present_outcome()` (exposed as `MainUI.report_outcome()`), which
routes a backend refusal through the same `present_error()` the rest of the rejection surface
uses.

issues.title: fix(ui): every response window now advertises the Attention it charges (the stray cat is 25 events)
issues.body:
Playtest 2026-08-10, Pip, on the stray cat: *"Adopting the cat also costs
attention, which is not advertised on the screen. Feeding it and shooing it away
also cost attention which is not on the screen."*

Two of those three are true, and the cause is not in the cat.

## What is actually happening

A **response window** levies `WindowResolver.attention_cost(event)` -- a price
that lives on the EVENT, not in any option's `costs` dict. `stray_cat` carries no
`window` block, so it takes `DEFAULT_ATTENTION_COST` (1). And
`EventTiers.tier_of()` classifies **any `"type": "popup"` with options** as a
window, so this is the whole popup surface: **25 events, 75 options** in
`core_events.json`, every one of them charging a founder hour the label never
mentioned.

`#1205` did the action bar. The event dialog is a different surface and the sweep
never reached it -- exactly the class the brief predicted.

Per-option, verified against the resolver rather than assumed:

| option | label before | actually charged |
|---|---|---|
| `adopt_cat` | ` ($500)` | $500 **+ 1 Attention** |
| `feed_and_release` | ` ($100)` | $100 **+ 1 Attention** |
| `shoo_away` | ` (Free)` | **nothing** -- correct |

`shoo_away` escapes because `ignore_option_id()` auto-picks the first option with
an empty `costs` dict, and that option resolves as IGNORE, which draws no
Attention. So the reported "all three" is two. Worth saying plainly: the free-out
is free *by auto-detection*, not by declaration -- give `shoo_away` a cost, or
give the event a `window.ignore_option`, and all three become HANDLEs at 1
Attention each.

## The half-kept promise

`strip_attention()`'s own docstring already said the point was that *"the dialog's
affordability display matches what resolution will actually charge"*. It only ever
did the erasing half -- it removed a declared Attention cost and never disclosed
the window's own. This PR writes the other half.

`WindowResolver.present_for_dialog()` is now what the two window emit sites hand
the presenter: `strip_attention()` plus the price stamped back on as display
metadata.

**Why stamp instead of recomputing in the UI.** The dialog is fed from **six**
`event_triggered` emit sites and only two of them strip. A stripped event is
indistinguishable from an un-stripped one whose options simply never declared
Attention, so the presenter *cannot* tell from the dict alone that a charge is
coming. Stamping at the one seam that knows makes every un-stamped path -- the
plan-phase legacy popups, the synthetic month review -- silently correct: no key,
no claim. There is a negative-control test for exactly that.

## Three options are deliberately NOT surcharged

Each for a reason that was checked, not assumed:

- **The free-out.** The resolver stamps *which* option resolves as IGNORE, so the
  label cannot drift from the charge. Mirroring `resolve_chosen_option`'s test
  verbatim is the whole point -- a hardcoded `"shoo_away"` in the UI would be the
  next bug.
- **An option whose own costs still carry `attention`** -- an un-stripped legacy
  event whose cost `format_cost_summary` already prints. Adding on top would show
  one charge as two.
- **`#789` hiring accept-prompts** (`window.option_verbs`), whose option text
  already names the price *and* the payment source: "Set them up now (2 Att from
  reserve)".

## Display only -- and the grey-out is left alone on purpose

The affordability grey-out is **not** wired to the new number. Window Attention is
paid **reserve-first**, and the dialog's affordability loop reads
`state.attention` = `get_available_attention()` = `total - spent - RESERVED`.
After a month commits, `GameManager` reserves the entire remainder
(`game_manager.gd:730`), so `available` is 0 while the reserve is full -- gating
on it would grey out **every window button in the game**. The number is now shown;
the engine stays the authority on whether it can be paid.

No cost was changed. Balance is Pip's.

## Tests

Eight, in `test_cost_display.gd` -- where the 2026-07-24 cost sweep already lives.
They lock the **disclosure, not the price**: each compares the label against
`WindowResolver`'s own accessors, so a rebalance moves both together and only a
*divergence* fails. Two are class-wide sweeps over every window-tier popup rather
than assertions about the cat.

**Negative control, run rather than asserted.** Stamping `0` instead of
`attention_cost(event)`:

```
1321 tests, 2 failures
  test_stray_cat_priced_options_advertise_the_window_attention
  test_every_charging_window_option_now_shows_attention
```

Restored:

```
python3 scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300
[TOTALS] quick: 1321 tests, 0 fail (ok)   130/130 files, exit 0
```

Baseline 1313 + these 8 = 1321.

## Found and NOT fixed here

Neither is display-only, so neither belongs in this PR. Both are in the
consolidated issue with the rest of the audit:

- **The conference trip tile renders "Free"** while the trip consumes *all*
  remaining Attention -- and re-charges at every month boundary crossed while
  away. `travel.json` sets `costs: {}` deliberately (`_seam` comment); the commit
  button is honest but non-numeric, the upstream tile is a flat lie.
- **Five hiring action-bar entries print "No costs"** for actions that spend 1-3
  Attention through the pipeline. Putting those numbers in the `costs` dicts would
  **double-charge**, because `game_manager` debits declared Attention at queue
  time. Needs a display channel, not a data edit.

`Ladder-Impact: none` -- presentation only. `present_for_dialog()` is additive and
used by nobody but the two dialog emit sites; `strip_attention()`,
`attention_cost()` and every payment path are untouched. The two extra keys ride
on the dialog's copy only, and the round trip back through
`resolve_current_window_option()` reads `event.id` and nothing else.

Stayed out of `_on_dynamic_action_pressed()`, `main_ui.gd` and
`submenu_controller.gd` entirely -- concurrent lanes.

issues.title: Attention spent without saying so: the 4 surfaces PR #1217 could not fix display-only, + the cat has no art SLOT (not a missing asset)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Follow-up to PR #1217, which fixed the reported case (the stray cat) and its whole
class (all 25 popup events). This is everything the same audit found that could
**not** be fixed display-only, filed together rather than as five thin issues.

The audit worked from the code, not the UI: every path that reaches
`MonthPlan.spend_attention()` / `can_spend_hours()` / `pay_by_cannibalizing()`,
traced back to what triggers it.

## Full audit result

Ranked by how likely a player is to hit it.

| # | Surface | Attention | Shown before commit? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Popup events / response windows** (25 events, 75 options -- incl. the stray cat) | 1 (`DEFAULT_ATTENTION_COST`) | **HIDDEN** -- and hidden after, too | **FIXED in #1217** |
| 2 | Action bar + icon-grid submenus (fundraising / publicity / strategic / operations / financing) | 1-2, declared in `costs` | SHOWN -- on-face cost label + tooltip + hover info bar | OK |
| 3 | Direct-hire actions (`hiring.json`, 7 of them) | 1, declared | SHOWN | OK |
| 4 | **Hiring action-bar entries** (`advertise`, `use_connections`, `interview_next`, `hire_best`, `onboard_next`) | 3 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1-2 each | **HIDDEN -- actively labelled "No costs"** | **Below, item A** |
| 5 | Hiring **panel** buttons (same five actions, different surface) | same | SHOWN on the button face | OK -- but see item A |
| 6 | **Conference trip** (travel submenu -> commit dialog) | **all remaining**, re-charged per month boundary while away | **tile says "Free"**; commit button says "all remaining Attention" but no number | **Below, item B** |
| 7 | Audit action (`operations.json`) | 1, `audits` kind | SHOWN | OK |
| 8 | `#789` hiring accept-prompt windows | 1-2 | SHOWN -- price *and* payment source in the option text | OK |
| 9 | Ledger attention-denominated bill | `entry.principal` | AUTOMATIC (no click) | **Below, item C** |
| 10 | `MediaSystem.execute_exclusive_interview` | 1 | UNREACHABLE -- zero callers | **Below, item D** |

**Counts: 1 HIDDEN fixed, 2 HIDDEN outstanding (items A and B), 1 automatic, 1
dead, 5 already correct.** Nothing landed in SHOWN LATE except the conference
trip's numeric figure, which appears post-commit in the vignette and the return
backlog panel.

---

## A. Five hiring actions print "No costs" and spend 1-3 Attention

`godot/data/actions/core.json` -- `advertise`, `use_connections`,
`interview_next`, `hire_best`, `onboard_next` all declare `"costs": {}`. The
hover info bar therefore renders `[color=gray]No costs[/color]`
(`main_ui.gd:2174`), and `action_bar_renderer`'s affordability check never greys
them out. They are not merely unlabelled -- they are **labelled free**.

What they actually spend, via `HiringPipeline`:

| action | Attention | source |
|---|---|---|
| `advertise` | 3 | `hiring.advertise.cost_attention` |
| `use_connections` | 2 | `hiring.connections.cost_attention` |
| `interview_next` | 2 | `hiring.interview.cost_attention` |
| `hire_best` | 1 | `hiring.offer.cost_attention` |
| `onboard_next` | 1-2 **per hire**, one click | `HiringPipeline.ONBOARD_ATTENTION` |

`onboard_next` is the sharp one: a single click auto-picks the next step for
*every* hire in flight, so with three hires cooking it can drain 3-6 Attention
with no number anywhere.

**Why this is not a data edit.** Putting `"attention": 3` into `advertise`'s
`costs` would **double-charge** -- `game_manager.gd:218-275` debits declared
Attention at queue time, and the pipeline debits again at execution time. The
`costs: {}` is load-bearing. This needs a display-only channel (the same shape as
#1217's stamp), not a JSON change.

Note the same five actions are already correct on the *hiring panel*, which puts
"Advertise\n($8k + 3 Att)" on the button face -- so the game shows the price on
one surface and denies it on another. Also worth a look while in there: those
panel labels are **hardcoded literals**, not read from `Balance`, so a retune
desyncs them silently. Two of the five (`systems`, `meet_people`) do read the
constant; the rest do not.

`hiring_panel_controller.gd` also uses none of the three shared cost helpers
(`_format_costs_inline`, `_costs_affordable`, `_make_cost_label`) that
`submenu_controller.gd` and `travel_panel_controller.gd` both use, and has no
cost-based affordability gating at all -- clicking with insufficient Attention
runs the delegate and surfaces a red log line after the fact.

## B. The conference trip tile says "Free"

`travel.json` -> `attend_conference_trip` has `"costs": {}` with a `_seam`
comment explaining why (the trip resolves synchronously at commit time, not
through the plan queue). Consequence:
`main_ui._format_costs_inline({})` returns `"Free"`, and the travel submenu
renders that on the tile face.

What it actually costs (`conference_trip.gd:280-286`): **every un-reserved
OPERATING hour you have left** --

```gdscript
var free: int = mini(
    state.month_plan.hours_available(MonthPlan.HOUR_OPERATING),
    state.month_plan.available()
)
```

-- and it is charged **again at every month boundary crossed while away**
(`conference_trip.gd:180`), so the fresh grant of the new month is wiped too.
That repeat drain is disclosed nowhere in the UI, only in a docstring.
`can_commit()` checks money only, never Attention.

The commit button is honest but non-numeric ("Commit -- $X + all remaining
Attention"). The tile that leads to it is the problem. A fix wants either a
display override on the tile or a projected figure on the commit button; the
number does exist at commit time.

Deliberately not attempted in #1217: it needs `main_ui.gd` /
`submenu_controller.gd`, both live in concurrent lanes this week.

## C. The ledger's attention bill has no cause-log entry

`ledger.gd:280-288` bills `int(e.principal)` OPERATING hours during
`tick_and_bill()`. It is the **only** currency branch in that switch that does not
call `_note(...)`, so it produces no `cause_log` attribution -- the player would
see the hours vanish with a single feed line and no trace in the breakdown.

Low urgency: **no live producer mints an attention-denominated entry today.**
Every factory (`Ledger.loan`, `funding_strings`, `desperation_payroll`,
`staff_rider`, `appetite_promise`, `FinanceEngine._standing_rider`,
`WindowResolver._mint_deferral`) mints money / governance / papers / compute /
equity. The branch is reachable only via `Ledger.from_dict` rehydration. Worth
fixing before anything starts minting them, not after.

## D. `MediaSystem` is dead code

`MediaSystem.execute_exclusive_interview` (`media_system.gd:232-246`) spends 1
OPERATING hour and has **zero callers**. The class is never instantiated,
`GameState` has no `media_system` member, and no `exclusive_interview` action id
exists in `godot/data/`. Only two comments reference it. Either wire it with a
declared cost or delete it -- as written, re-wiring it as-is would ship another
hidden charge (its only Attention disclosure is a rejection string).

---

## E. Separate, and a different owner: the stray cat renders with no art

Reported in the same playtest: *"Stray cat appearing doesn't have any graphics on
it yet despite having assets in the queue."*

**Verdict: neither a missing-asset problem nor an unpromoted-asset problem.**
It is a third thing, and it matters because it means neither the art owner nor
`#1166`'s share-set route can fix it.

**There is no slot to promote art INTO.** Three independent checks:

1. **No art field exists on the event schema.** Union of every key used across all
   25 events in `godot/data/events/core_events.json`: `id`, `name`, `description`,
   `type`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_turn`, `trigger_condition`, `repeatable`,
   `options`, `probability`, `min_turn`, `cooldown_turns`, `extra_condition`.
   Option level: `id`, `text`, `costs`, `effects`, `message`. No image, icon,
   texture, art or portrait key anywhere.
2. **The presenter cannot render one.** `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd` is 497
   lines and builds its panel entirely in code. It contains **zero** matches for
   `texture|sprite|image|.png|.svg|.jpg` -- there is no `TextureRect` in the
   dialog at all.
3. **The demand manifest is empty.** ADR-0019 makes packing demand-gated ("the
   only path into `godot/assets/` is a mechanically verified demand entry"), and
   `tools/assets/demand/slot_picks.json` currently has `"slots": {}`. There is no
   demand entry that could pull a cat into an event popup, and none could be
   written, because there is no slot.

Meanwhile the art is not the constraint. Cat art is abundant in `art_source/`
(eight-plus pixellab cat directories) and some is **already packed**:
`godot/assets/cats/simple/` holds 8 live photos and `assets/images/office_cat.png`
is referenced by `main.tscn`. But that art belongs to the **office cat widget**
(`office_cat.gd`, the persistent decoration + credits surface), which is a
different consumer from the encounter.

So the owner here is **engineering, not art**: an art channel on the event popup
(schema field + a `TextureRect` in `event_dialog.gd` + a demand slot) has to exist
*before* promotion is even a question. Filed here as the finding; no art was
touched.

---

Audit method, so it can be re-run: start from `grep -rn "spend_attention\|can_spend_hours\|pay_by_cannibalizing"`
over `godot/scripts/`, then trace each site back to its trigger and forward to its
presenting UI.

issues.title: ci(guard): detect a stale Godot class cache -- the failure CI structurally cannot see

labels.name: testing
labels.description: Issues related to test suite and testing infrastructure

labels.name: class:guard
labels.description: Adds or repairs a check, gate or CI condition. Self-merge on green with a recorded RED run.

issues.body:
Closes #1215. Guard only -- **the incident itself is already fixed** (`godot --headless --path godot --import`, confirmed working). This builds the thing that would have caught it.

**Not for the release cut.** Tooling and docs only; nothing under `godot/` changes and no game code is touched. `Ladder-Impact: none -- tooling and docs only, no file under godot/ changed.`

## What broke

`godot/.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg` is **generated, gitignored and per-checkout**. `#1211` added `class_name Capacity` from a separate worktree, which built its own fresh cache and passed 1313 tests. The shared checkout only pulled, so its cache predated the file. Every dependent script failed to parse -- and the game still launched, drew the background art and the doom readout, and then did nothing, in front of a first-time playtester. Full symptom record and the verbatim capture are in #1215.

## Why this cannot be a CI gate

CI clones fresh every run, so it always generates a correct cache. **Only a long-lived working copy can hold a stale one.** The guard therefore lives on the launch path. CI's only job here is to prove the *detector* still works.

## The check

`tools/check_class_cache.py` -- pure Python, no Godot launch, **~30ms over 364 `.gd` files**. Every `class_name X` in `godot/**/*.gd` must match, name and path, an entry in the cache. Reports `MISSING` / `MOVED` / `ORPHANED`.

## RED runs (observed, per estate 5g)

RED-RUN: https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/31768503202 -- hardwired `is_stale()` to return False, the exact way a guard rots; the CI detector-self-test went red on `test_red_on_the_incident_shape` (`FAILED (failures=6)`). Reverted in `f0308415`.

That run proves the **CI step** is load-bearing. The run below proves the **detector** catches the real condition -- both are needed, because CI can never produce a stale cache itself.

### The real condition, locally

On a scratch worktree at `origin/main`, with a real generated cache, removing the single `Capacity` record -- i.e. reconstructing the 2026-08-13 cache exactly: correct about all 95 other classes, silent about the one that mattered.

**1. Baseline GREEN**
```
$ python3 tools/check_class_cache.py
class cache OK -- 96 class_name declaration(s) all resolve.        # exit 0
```

**2. Stale it, and the check goes RED**
```
$ python3 stale_it.py godot/.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg Capacity
removed 1 record for Capacity from .../global_script_class_cache.cfg

$ python3 tools/check_class_cache.py
STALE CLASS CACHE -- this checkout will run the WRONG code, silently.
  1 class_name(s) declared in source but NOT in the cache.
    MISSING   Capacity                         res://scripts/core/capacity.gd
  FIX:  godot --headless --path godot --import                     # exit 1
```

**3. The staled cache reproduces the real failure** -- so the check is not detecting a synthetic condition:
```
$ godot-iso cacheguard godot --headless --path godot --quit
  30  x  Parse Error: Identifier "Capacity" not declared in the current scope.
  17  x  Compile Error: Failed to compile depended scripts.
  godot exit = 0          <-- NOTE
```
Dead scripts included `game_manager.gd`, `game_state.gd`, `month_controller.gd`, `turn_manager.gd` (no active game, phase stuck on *starting up*, cannot commit the month), `actions.gd` and `upgrades.gd` (no icons, no upgrades), plus 3 autoloads. That maps 1:1 onto what the playtester saw.

**That `exit 0` is the finding that changed the wiring.** `godot --headless --path godot --quit` is `make lint`, and it was green through the whole cascade. So `make lint` now depends on the class-cache target too.

**4. Repair, and it goes GREEN**
```
$ godot-iso cacheguard python3 tools/check_class_cache.py --repair
STALE CLASS CACHE -- ...
    MISSING   Capacity                         res://scripts/core/capacity.gd
  repairing: godot --headless --path godot --import
repaired -- 96 class_name declaration(s) now resolve.              # exit 0

$ godot-iso cacheguard godot --headless --path godot --quit
  0  x  Parse Error ...
  0  x  Compile Error ...
```

`tests/test_check_class_cache.py` (18 tests, all green) pins this as a fixture so the detector cannot decay into a function that always returns 0.

## Where it is wired

| Where | Mode | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `make run` | auto-repair | The launch path. Where the failure bites. |
| `make lint` | auto-repair | Makes an existing gate honest -- see the `exit 0` above. |
| pre-commit `post-merge` / `post-checkout` | warn only | The exact moment a working copy goes stale: `git pull`. |
| `quality-checks.yml` | blocking unit tests | Proves the detector, since CI cannot produce the condition. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | doc | "Run the game" now says `make run`, not bare `godot --path godot`. |

**Auto-repair over refusal**, chosen deliberately. The fix is mechanical with no judgement call, so refusing to launch is just a slower path to the same command. The stronger reason: the failure looks like a game that is still loading, so a warning behind a plausible-looking window is not a guard. Auto-repair turns a silent, mystifying failure into a named, self-healing one.

**Not a pre-commit hook**, also deliberately. The machine that authors a new `class_name` always has a fresh cache; a commit-time gate watches the one place that is never wrong.

## Two things needing Pip's call

**1. `godot-iso` was not the playtest path.** The brief suggested wiring the guard there. Reading `~/.local/bin/godot-iso` first, it says in its own header:

> `# DO NOT use this for playtesting -- a real playtest SHOULD write to the real profile, or the score does not count and the league board never sees it.`

So a guard there would **not** have caught this incident. It is still worth having as a second layer for agent lanes and headless runs, and the proposed diff is below -- but the wiring that actually covers the incident is `make run`.

**2. `~/.local/bin/godot-iso` is outside the repo. I did NOT edit it.** Proposed diff, inserted after the mtime snapshot so the existing isolation guarantee is unaffected, with the repair running **inside** `XDG_DATA_HOME` so an auto-import cannot touch the real profile:

```diff
@@ -45,6 +45,32 @@
 # snapshot the real profile's mtimes so we can PROVE it was not written to
 before=$(find "$REAL" -type f -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort | sha256sum)

+# --- stale class-cache pre-flight (2026-08-13 incident; see tools/check_class_cache.py) ---
+# godot/.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg is generated, gitignored and PER-CHECKOUT. A
+# long-lived working copy can hold one that predates a pulled `class_name`, and then every
+# dependent script fails to parse while Godot still EXITS 0. Measured on the incident's own
+# shape: 30 parse errors, 17 depended-script compile failures, exit status 0. So a run under
+# this wrapper can report a clean isolation proof over a build that is silently not the code.
+#
+# Deliberately INSIDE the isolation: the repair is a Godot --import, so it runs with
+# XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at the sandbox like everything else. The mtime digest above is
+# already taken, so the existing "real profile untouched" guarantee still covers it.
+#
+# Non-fatal by design: this wrapper's job is isolation, not correctness gating. If the repair
+# cannot happen (no Godot, no checkout) it says so and runs the command anyway.
+if [ -f tools/check_class_cache.py ]; then
+    set +e
+    XDG_DATA_HOME="$SANDBOX" python3 tools/check_class_cache.py --repair --quiet
+    cache_rc=$?
+    set -e
+    if [ $cache_rc -ne 0 ]; then
+        echo "godot-iso: *** class cache is STALE and could not be repaired ***" >&2
+        echo "godot-iso: this run may execute code whose class_names do not resolve." >&2
+        echo "godot-iso: fix with: godot --headless --path godot --import" >&2
+        echo >&2
+    fi
+fi
+
 set +e
 XDG_DATA_HOME="$SANDBOX" "$@"
 rc=$?
```

The proposed version was **run from the scratchpad, not installed**, against a deliberately staled cache. It detected, repaired, ran the command, and the existing guarantee still held:

```
godot-iso: lane 'cacheguard'
STALE CLASS CACHE -- ...
    MISSING   Capacity                         res://scripts/core/capacity.gd
repaired -- 96 class_name declaration(s) now resolve.
4.5.1.stable.official.f62fdbde1
godot-iso: real profile untouched (verified by mtime digest)     <-- non-regression
```

To install: `cp /tmp/claude-1000/-home-pip/d2a42750-061c-4dbf-851b-b445da5210dc/scratchpad/godot-iso.proposed /home/pip/.local/bin/godot-iso`

**One more thing that is inert until installed:** the `post-merge` / `post-checkout` hook needs, once per checkout:
`pre-commit install --hook-type post-merge --hook-type post-checkout`

## Verification

```
python3 -m unittest tests.test_check_class_cache      # Ran 18 tests -- OK
python3 tools/check_class_cache.py                    # exit 0, 96 declarations resolve
pre-commit validate-config .pre-commit-config.yaml    # CONFIG OK  (pre-commit 4.2.0)
make class-cache                                      # exit 0
bash -n godot-iso.proposed                            # syntax OK
```

Also regenerated, because their `--check` hooks gate the commit and the new dated prose feeds them: `docs/TOOLS.md`, `docs/calendar/`.

Not touched: `art_generated/`, `art_prompts/`, `tools/art_review/`. No `.import` / `.uid` churn was staged.

issues.title: Stale generated per-checkout artefact: a cache Godot needs, git cannot ship, and CI cannot see

labels.name: testing
labels.description: Issues related to test suite and testing infrastructure

labels.name: class:guard
labels.description: Adds or repairs a check, gate or CI condition. Self-merge on green with a recorded RED run.

issues.body:
## The class of failure

**A generated, gitignored, per-checkout artefact is required for correctness, and nothing that starts from a clean slate can tell you yours is wrong.**

On 2026-08-13 this cost a playtest with a first-time player in front of the machine.

`#1211` added `godot/scripts/core/capacity.gd` declaring `class_name Capacity`. Godot resolves every `class_name` through `godot/.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg`, which is generated by the engine, gitignored, and belongs to one checkout. The agent that wrote `#1211` worked in a separate worktree, which built its own fresh cache. **1313 tests passed there.** The shared checkout only *pulled*, so its cache predated the new file, and every script depending on `Capacity` died:

```
SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Identifier "Capacity" not declared in the current scope.
SCRIPT ERROR: Compile Error: Failed to compile depended scripts.
```

Reproduced on a scratch copy on 2026-08-14 by removing the one `Capacity` record from a good cache: **30 parse errors, 17 depended-script compile failures, across `game_manager.gd`, `game_state.gd`, `month_controller.gd`, `turn_manager.gd`, `actions.gd`, `upgrades.gd`, `doom_system.gd`, `events.gd`, `save_load.gd` and 3 autoloads.**

## What the player saw

Not an error. Not a dialog. Not a crash. A game that looked like it had not finished loading. Pip, narrating at the machine while the playtester sat there (capture `2026-08-13_214820__db1ee7a2`, on `e44660c4`):

> *"the game appears to have lost all its icons... normally, there are icons along the top somewhere, in a horizontal row, that you can click on to take actions, and there's not normally a cat there"*
>
> *"it says phase starting up"*
>
> *"I'm trying to get to plan mode, and it says for each action, click the actions below them, I've got research quality, rushed, standard, thorough, and... all my icons have disappeared. And all my upgrades have disappeared, and I can't commit the month, and the music track seems not to be working, and also, there's no active game, so I don't think the game's actually initialized, because we still have a cat on the starting screen"*

| Still worked | Dead |
| --- | --- |
| Window, background art (a cat) | Every action icon |
| Doom readout at 58.5% | Every upgrade |
| `phase: starting up` label | Commit-month |
| Research-quality selector (rushed / standard / thorough) | Music |
| | Game initialisation -- the phase never advanced past *starting up* |

**The partial render is the trap.** Enough of the UI survives that the screen is plausible. Anyone would assume it was still loading and wait. Diagnosis needed a headless run to surface the parse errors the windowed run swallowed.

Fix was `godot --headless --path godot --import`. Seconds, mechanical, unambiguous. **Already applied; this issue is the permanent record, not an open fault.**

## Why CI is structurally incapable of catching it

CI clones fresh every run, so it *always* generates a correct cache. **Only a long-lived working copy can hold a stale one.** Every check that starts clean is blind to this by construction, and most checks start clean.

Two measured facts that make it worse:

1. **`godot --headless --path godot --quit` EXITS 0** through the entire cascade. That is `make lint`. "It did not crash" and "the process exited 0" are both worthless signals here.
2. The already-documented sibling trap in `CLAUDE.md` -- *"GUT quits(0) if the class cache is cold"* -- is the **loud** half. Cold means absent, and it fails immediately and visibly. **Stale means present, plausible, and wrong about exactly the file someone just added.** Stale is the worse half and was undocumented until now.

## The guard

`tools/check_class_cache.py` -- pure Python, no Godot launch, **~30ms over 364 `.gd` files**. Every `class_name X` declared in `godot/**/*.gd` must match, name *and* path, an entry in the cache. Three findings: `MISSING` (the `#1211` shape), `MOVED` (a rename the cache did not see), `ORPHANED` (a deletion it did not see).

Wired at the moment of risk rather than the moment of commit:

| Where | Mode | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `make run` | auto-repair | The launch path. Where the failure bites. |
| `make lint` | auto-repair | Makes an existing gate honest -- see fact (1) above. |
| pre-commit `post-merge` / `post-checkout` | warn only | The exact moment a working copy goes stale: `git pull`. A merge cannot be undone and a pull should not block for a Godot import. |
| `quality-checks.yml` | blocking unit tests | CI cannot test the *condition*; it can prove the *detector* has not decayed into a function that always returns 0 (the #640 lesson). |
| `~/.local/bin/godot-iso` | auto-repair, non-fatal | Proposed, outside the repo -- covers agent lanes and headless runs. |

**Auto-repair, not refusal.** There is no judgement call in the fix, so refusing to launch would only be a slower route to the same command -- and the argument is stronger than convenience: the failure mode is *a screen that looks like it is still loading*. A warning printed to a terminal that nobody is looking at, behind a game window that seems to be working, is not a guard. Auto-repair converts a silent, mystifying failure into a named, self-healing one. That conversion is most of the value here.

**Deliberately NOT a pre-commit hook.** The machine that authors a new `class_name` always has a fresh cache. A commit-time gate would be watching the one place that is never wrong.

## Where this shape recurs

Anywhere a generated per-checkout artefact is load-bearing for correctness and gitignored. Known neighbours in this repo, all worth the same question -- *can a long-lived checkout hold a wrong one, and would anything notice?*

- `godot/.godot/` more broadly (import metadata, UID cache) -- the export-cache half of this is already handled by `build_release.py` nuking the directory.
- `godot/.import/`
- Generated indexes (`docs/TOOLS.md`, `DQ_INDEX.md`, ADR index, commitment calendar) -- these are the *safe* pattern, because they are tracked and gated by a `--check` hook. The contrast is instructive: the anti-rot pattern works when the artefact is in git. It cannot work when the artefact is gitignored by necessity, and that is when you need a launch-time guard instead.

issues.title: Half-day workshop: the first ten turns -- a first-timer could not tell what to do, and 44 -> 87 proves the surface is responsive, not that it is finished

labels.name: strategic
labels.description: Strategic planning and high-level architectural decisions
